claim: Eight economists, legal experts, and technologists filed an amicus brief in the D.C. Circuit on August 4, 2026, supporting the DOJ and state plaintiffs' cross-appeal in United States v. Google, arguing the district court's remedy should be strengthened.
stance_target: the DOJ/states' cross-appeal seeking a stronger search-monopoly remedy
scope_conditions: D.C. Circuit appeal of US v. Google search case, filed August 4, 2026
quoted_support: eight leading economists, legal experts, and technologists filed an amicus brief in the D.C. Circuit supporting the Department of Justice and State plaintiffs' cross-appeal and urging the Court to strengthen the remedy in the landmark search monopolization case.

claim: The amicus brief argues that the district court's remedy leaves Google's exclusionary strategy largely intact because Google can still pay for default placement on every device, so new entrants -- including AI companies -- cannot match Google's payments and cannot gain the distribution scale needed to compete, and the ordered data-sharing/syndication measures do not overcome this.
stance_target: insufficiency of Mehta's remedy absent a payment restriction
scope_conditions: US v. Google appellate amicus brief, D.C. Circuit, filed Aug 2026
quoted_support: Google's monopoly profits allow it to outbid any rival: As long as Google can continue paying for default placement on every device, new entrants – including AI companies – will not be able to match Google's payments... The current remedy leaves Google's exclusionary strategy largely intact: ...those measures cannot overcome the fact that competitors still lack meaningful default access to users if Google can continue purchasing the most valuable distribution channels.
